applicable_when: The kernel is severely bottlenecked by shared memory bank conflicts (8-way, 69.89% of shared load wavefronts) and uncoalesced shared accesses (67% excessive wavefronts), together worth ~59% potential speedup. These stem from: (1) the B-matrix load using a broadcast_to pattern that creates non-contiguous shared memory access, (2) BLOCK_K=32 being too small forcing 32 K-loop iterations for K=1024 with poor data reuse. Additionally, 168 registers/thread limits occupancy to 18.75% theoretical and only 6.25% achieved (4 warps/SM), leaving 69.53% of scheduler cycles with no eligible warp. The grid of 128 blocks is below the 132 SM count, leaving some SMs idle. On H200 (Hopper), TMA descriptors offload address generation to dedicated hardware, enabling asynchronous bulk copies that bypass the scalar pointer arithmetic causing the bank-conflict pattern.
